```{r}
#| include: false
# Exercise 1, part c: one numeric gap (extype: num) with a margin of 0.01; its label is the
# one-line Answerlist. ANS imports no model answer for a fill-in question, so the builder puts
# the solution in as feedback. The key is computed from the data, never typed in.
```

```{r data, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
f <- "ssr-furniture.csv"
d <- read.csv(if (file.exists(f)) f else file.path(exams:::.exams_get_internal("xexams_dir_exercises"), f))
suppressMessages(library(car))
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
d$instruction <- factor(d$instruction); d$age <- factor(d$age)
fp <- function(p) if (p < .001) "< .001" else paste("=", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
full  <- Anova(lm(minutes ~ instruction * age, d), type = 3)
msRes <- full["Residuals", "Sum Sq"] / full["Residuals", "Df"]; dfRes <- full["Residuals", "Df"]
msIns <- full["instruction", "Sum Sq"] / full["instruction", "Df"]
Fins  <- full["instruction", "F value"]; pIns <- full["instruction", "Pr(>F)"]
stopifnot(pIns < .001, isTRUE(all.equal(Fins, msIns / msRes)))
```

Question
========
What is the *F*-value of the main effect of the type of instruction? Use 2 decimals.

Answerlist
----------
* *F*-value:

Solution
========
In the ANOVA table in JASP, the row for instruction gives *F*(`r full["instruction", "Df"]`, `r dfRes`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", Fins)`, *p* `r fp(pIns)`. The *F*-value is the mean square of instruction divided by the residual mean square, `r sprintf("%.4f", msIns)` / `r sprintf("%.4f", msRes)` = `r sprintf("%.2f", Fins)`.

Lecture 17, slide 25 (Using mean squares to compute *F*).
